blocking.problem: SS18.2 says a standalone adj computes Co-loop flags 'from preserved trajectory inputs' with 'bounded trace reconstruction for overwritten conditions'. In general no such reconstruction from the adjoint-entry state exists: 'while (@x == 1) { @x ^= 1; @z += 1 }' maps (x,z) = (1,0) and (0,1) both to (0,1) with different trip counts, so the exit state does not determine the trajectory or flags. Basis witness B2 = 'while (@x < 2) { @x += 1; @z += 1 }' with @x,@z Co in basis state (2,2): reading A (flags computed from live-ins at adjoint application: c_1 is (2<2) = false) runs no inverse iteration and leaves (2,2); reading B (reconstruct an assumed forward run, e.g. entry (0,0)) runs two inverse iterations and gives (0,0). Same program, different classical memory. The lifetime is also contradictory: TDL-10 gives conditions/flags TDL-8 retained lifetime, SS18.2 uncomputes the adjoint's flags in reverse.
blocking.fix: Replace the Co-loop adjoint paragraph in SS18.2 with: 'In a standalone adj(f), a Co loop's conditions and flags are computed forward from the loop live-in values as they stand when adjoint(E) begins to apply, by forward trajectory simulation on copies of those live-ins. That simulated trajectory is a declared output of the adj invocation with TDL-8 lifetime; conditions and flags are uncomputed against it after the inverse iterations i = N..1. No trajectory of any earlier forward invocation is reconstructed. adj therefore inverts a Co loop on data alone only inside compute (same trajectory and flag wires) or when every condition input is a wire or byte the body does not modify (the ISA SS4.6 form); every other standalone adj has the adjoint-entry flag meaning just defined.' Delete 'bounded trace reconstruction'. Add state=co-loop-adj-overwritten: B2 at (@x,@z) = (2,2) under standalone adj gives (2,2), no trap. Alternative: reject standalone adj of bodies whose Co-loop condition reads body-written bytes (BD-E-COHERENT-LOOP-ADJ); I would take the defined-meaning text above because it keeps the capability and matches 'E generated from the current state, apply adjoint(E)' (TDL-6/SS18.3).

blocking.problem: The placement of the fresh deferred-record qcopy in standalone adj is only constrained to be 'before every adjointed event that depends on it' / 'before their first reversed consumer'. Take E = [qcopy a -> w, cx w t, h a]; adjoint(E) applies [h a, cx w t] plus the record. Placement (i) qcopy first copies the adj-entry a (post-h in the forward timeline); placement (ii) qcopy immediately before cx copies a after the adjointed h. I checked by statevector simulation: with adj applied at a = t = |0>, then H(a) and measure(a), placement (i) gives P(0) = 1 and placement (ii) gives P(0) = 1/2. Two conformant plugins produce different Born probabilities.
blocking.fix: In SS18.2 state: 'standalone adj(f) emits each deferred-measurement qcopy immediately before (in application order) the first adjointed event that depends on it, i.e. after every adjointed event that precedes that consumer; records first consumed by the same event are copied in their original order in E.' Add state=deferred-channel-adj-place: body = deferred measure of a, branch gate cx w t, h a; invoked by adj with a = t = |0>, then H(a), measure(a) gives P(0) = P(1) = 1/2, no trap. The alternative pin (all record copies at the start of adjoint(E), giving P(0) = 1 above) is also definable; I would take immediately-before because it copies the source at the reversed position closest to the original qcopy and yields the consumer-time wire whenever nothing between qcopy and its consumer in E touches the source.

blocking.section: SS10 TDL-2 (coverage), TDL-11 (store after partial observe, observe completion); SS18.2 last-but-one paragraph
blocking.problem: TDL-2: 'Coverage is tracked since each byte's last write; writes invalidate coverage.' SS18.2: 'Writes invalidate observation coverage.' TDL-11 observe: 'When every byte of X is covered since its last write ... K(X) = Cl.' But the new TDL-11 store rule says a CC store to covered bytes will 'retain that coverage'. Witness: X a 2-byte Co object; observe(p,1); CC store byte 0 = 9; observe(p+1,1); CC load byte 0. Retain reading: byte 0 stays covered, the second observe completes X, K = Cl, load returns 9. Invalidate reading: the store is a write, byte 0 is uncovered since it, K stays Co, the load traps T-TAINT-HOST code 4. Trap versus value on the same program.
blocking.fix: Pin one rule; I would take the retain reading that TDL-11 already promises. Add to TDL-2: 'Writes invalidate coverage, except a CC store permitted by TDL-11 to already-covered bytes: it writes a known classical value to the arena cells and shadow together, so those bytes remain covered, with that store as their covering write.' Change SS18.2 to 'Event-application writes invalidate observation coverage.' and the observe completion clause to 'covered since its last write other than such a CC store'. Add state=co-observe-write-observe for the witness above: after the second observe K = Cl, load of byte 0 returns 9, code 0. (The invalidate-and-reobserve default is equally implementable if the maintainer prefers one uniform coverage bit, but one of the two must be stated.)

blocking.section: SS6.5 (reference instance bound, setjmp preamble and rule 2); SS7.5(b)
blocking.problem: The new setjmp preamble is function-local ('if F contains a setjmp site'), but re-entry is interprocedural, and E(c) for call sites in rule 2 is never defined (which module/CFG, whether N29 continuation edges count as loop back edges). Witness: P() { r = setjmp(jb); G(r); ... } where G(i) { h = qalloc(0,1); store h into @slot[i]; deep(); } and deep() longjmps to jb on its first call. The site s is in G, which contains no setjmp; on the source call graph of SS4.1 (no longjmp edges) E(s) = 1 x E(callsite in P) = 1, so N(s) = 1. Execution allocates instance 1 into slot[0], longjmps, and allocates instance 2 into slot[1] while instance 1 is live (native check with clang -O2, LLVM 18 and 23: slots = 1,2, max live = 2). The N = 1 plugin must alias the live register or trap where the reference semantics has two clean handles; a second plugin that counts materialised sjlj cycles gets E = infinity and verdict blocked:BD-B-ISA4, so even the module verdict diverges. SS7.5(b) R hoisting inherits the gap.
blocking.fix: Replace the SS6.5 preamble with an interprocedural rule and define E(c): 'Before rules 1-2, augment each CFG with an N29 edge from every call in whose closure a longjmp may execute to the continuation of every setjmp site in every function that may be an ancestor of that call in the call graph. E(c) for a call site c is the product of the constant maximum trip counts of the loops of the augmented CFG of c's function that contain c, times the sum of E over the call sites of that function (device entry = 1), and is infinity if any such loop has no constant maximum trip count. The reference default remains conservative: if the continuation of a setjmp site in any may-ancestor A of F (A = F included) can reach s through augmented CFG and call edges, s is not self-disjoint and E(s) = infinity (BLK-1; BLK-4 under SS7.5(b)), with the bounded static-file fallback.' Add example=handle-setjmp-interproc for the witness above with verdict=blocked:BD-B-ISA4 and state {instances: 2, distinct: true, live_after: 0, trap: 0} under the 64-instance fallback.
